findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

Focused reviewability: pass. The plan opens with a clear mental model (contract → clean snapshot → detached clone → fixed runner → exact reconciliation → authenticated external store, with a read-only verifier), and every load-bearing decision is in the main path. It covers all 12 scenario blocks (17 cases), the one affected surface, and the SWM persona. Architecture, data, measurement, rollout, rollback and doc impact are each decided, with reasons. The durable architecture link resolves, and the case-to-assertion map matches the actual Vitest test names and their expanded parameter rows. One blocking defect remains. The plan has no real-boundary proof that the shipped 37-case profile actually succeeds against the real T3E4NS lane in the real repository. Its own riskiest assumption could therefore be wrong while every planned check passes. The success proof also does not settle how the observer's nested Vitest run interacts with the global test lock. Four warnings follow.

Proof quality, @demo scenario 'Complete fixed-lane execution produces verifiable current evidence' and the R2 success threshold. The plan names its riskiest assumption: the shipped profile must identify every real required assertion and parameter row. The proof table does not commit to testing that against the real lane. The 'Complete proof' row names only 'real CLI, fixed runner, complete raw report'. A separate paragraph says integration controls run 'committed fixture source at the fixed paths' through the unmodified runner. Row 1 cites the 'real shipped profile', but scenario 1 never requires a successful observation. Under this plan, an implementation could prove success only on fixture test files that copy the profile's tuples. The shipped profile could then disagree with the real report's identities (for example how Vitest formats describe/full names, `%s` or `$label` placeholders, or top-level `it` names), or fail on the real Codex/plugin tests. Every planned check would still pass, but the maintainer's first real observation would refuse, so the accepted claim is broken. The assertion map was checked only against an earlier retained characterization, which the plan itself says is not a new run. A second gap is that the plan says the existing global test lock serializes real Vitest processes. It does not decide whether an observer started inside a Vitest-run integration test, which itself launches the runner, can take that lock or will deadlock. That gap may be exactly why fixtures were chosen. Owner: Implementation Planning (agent). Required decision: name the real-boundary proof that runs the shipped profile through the installed or source CLI against the actual committed repository candidate, requiring success and the exact-once 37-case reconciliation. This may be a separate verification-lane run outside the Vitest suite if nesting is unsafe. State how lock nesting is avoided and the remaining confidence limit. Consequence if unresolved: profile-to-real-…

Independent completeness oracle. The data architecture guide's independent-proof module applies, because the plan claims exact 37-case completeness. The profile carries both the case inventory and the mappings. The plan does not explicitly say that admission recompiles the committed T3E4NS feature and grades its case IDs and digests as an exact set against the profile, refusing missing, extra or changed cases. Without that, a self-consistent but incomplete profile (with both the case and its mapping removed) could pass. Today only reviewer care at contract-update time prevents this. State that the compiled feature is the independent oracle and that it is recomputed at admission and at verification.

The PlanEvidenceRecordV1 entries set license, attribution, security and reuse limits to 'none_declared'. But the plan's own table states security boundaries ('documentation is not sandbox protection'; 'same-user signing authority remains trusted'), and the prose notes that installed Vitest declares MIT. The plan says these fields record what the source page declares, but readers of the records could take them as 'no limit'. Consider recording the plan's actual security limits in security_limit, or state explicitly in each record that limits are documented in the adjacent table.

Currency may be hard to keep in practice. The whole tracked product tree is bound, the clean-tree check applies at verification, and phase_anchors and all non-Work-Log body text in both tickets are bound. As a result, any unrelated commit, any ledger or review-ledger write, or a phase transition that adds an anchor will stale the observation. This is conservative and allowed by R4, and the assessment triggers acknowledge that certification consumers may stale their own evidence. The plan should still state where the certification consumer is expected to verify (before any ledger write) so the evidence is current when it is needed. Also confirm that binding the observer ticket PPHQN5 (rather than only T3E4NS) is intended, because its own later phase transitions will stale every observation.

Proportionality (deletion test). Several passages are execution-level detail that could move to Execution Planning without losing any decision: the 32-byte key and 0700/0600 modes, the full tool list (tar, mise, shell utilities), the build-lock runner mechanics, and the step-by-step clone preparation. Keep the decisions (separate key, bound tool inventory, controlled PATH, verified dependency-tree copy) and let Execution Planning carry the mechanics.

Verified against context. Every full name in the proposed assertion map matches the supplied test sources, including top-level `it` names, interpolated `$label` names and printf `%s` names, and both declaration orders for the fallback cases. The feature compiles to 12 blocks and 17 cases, as the plan states. The architecture link resolves to the Proposed 'Bounded observation preserves completion authority' record. Data applicability covers all 11 subjects, and the source-of-truth and owner statements do not conflict. Measurement has a reasoned skip.

Context discrepancy, not a plan defect. ticket.md's plan-implementation phase anchor points at the feature file rather than impl-plan.md, and the Work Log ends before the restored scenario review 79aecfba that the plan cites; implementation-review.md does record that review.
